text:
DevOps-bot: nightly-perf-alert | run=3832104567 | suite=small-batch | model=redwood-v1-7b | quant=q4_0 | p95:+31% | alert_id=NP-3832

Maria: saw the alert. p95 for small-batch drifted from ~82ms -> ~108ms on the nightly harness. CI artifacts: https://ci.redwood.internal/3832104567/artifacts

Sam: thanks. any obvious infra flakiness? node warm? GPU temp?

DevOps-bot: node snapshot attached: s3://ci-traces/3832104567/node.tar.gz. no ECC, GPU util normal.

Lee: i can repro on my workstation: `./bench --model redwood-v1-7b --quant q4_0 --batch 2 --seq 256 --iters 60` -> p95 ~110ms. baseline on my box ~80ms. quick perf snippet attached.

Carmen: if you can repro, please capture `nsys` and `strace -f -tt` for one iteration; curious if kernel scheduling or extra memcpy calls show up. also grab `top -H` to see thread-level cpu spin.

Lee: uploaded nsys: s3://ci-traces/3832104567/lee_nsys.nsys and strace: s3://ci-traces/3832104567/lee_strace.log

Nate: quick metrics idea  check runtime.batch.queue_time_ms and batcher.lock_hold_ms. if lock hold went up, more serialization could explain p95 tail.

Maria: dashboard shows batcher.lock_hold_ms p95 spiked around the same time as nightly run. batch queue_time also up slightly. commit range for suspects: last-green..HEAD includes 3b7c9a1 (scheduler refactor) and 4e2f11b (batched-prep cache).

Sam: i'm starting a light bisect. will try to run bench against selected commits and report back.

Lee: fwiw, running with env var `RW_BATCHER_PREEMPT=0` reduces p95 to ~86ms locally. that might be a quick mitigator to test on CI.

Carmen: interesting. nsys shows extra cpu-side spin in `batcher::prepare()` in the refactor build; multiple small memcpy calls land in hot path. kernel durations stable. looks CPU-bound on main thread.

Nate: filing a quick monitoring alert to watch batcher.lock_hold_ms on dedicated-nightly canary. if canary passes we can merge revert+fix. putting rule in place now.

Sam: bisect update: first bad commit is 3b7c9a1 (scheduler refactor). reproduces when checked out. opening PR to revert the scheduler portion: https://git.redwood/runtime/pull/501

Maria: thanks. plan: land revert in a canary branch -> kick dedicated-nightly -> watch p95 and batcher metrics -> if fixed, merge to main. Carmen, can you add the memcpy stack traces to the perf ticket? Lee, add repro steps and the env var mitigation.

Carmen: will attach flamegraph + stack traces to ticket PERF-1298. observed stack root: batcher::prepare -> memcpy -> pthread_spin_lock in some cases.

DevOps-bot: triggered dedicated-nightly canary job: https://ci.redwood.internal/3832104567/canary. status: queued.

Maria: pinging @eng-sre for visibility. if canary fails, we'll page.

Sam: quick note for next steps: after revert lands we should run microbench with combinatorial flags (prefetch on/off, preempt 0/1) to ensure we don't regress other paths. I'll add a matrix to the PR.

Nate: monitoring rule live. will escalate if p95 stays >+20% after canary.

Maria: thanks team. i'll summarize in the morning and close the loop.
